PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 3
-- UK GROUP IN 1.1 BILLION STG HEALTHCARE DEAL

UK private equity specialist Cinven has finalised a 1.1bn stg deal to acquire the UK and French hospital and healthcare interests of French conglomerate Compagnie Generale des Eaux. In the UK, Cinven will pay 570m stg for General Healthcare Group, which it plans to merge with Amicus healthcare, while in France Generale de Sante is being sold for 360m stg. The acquisition represents the largest management buy-out since 1989's 2.4bn stg Gateway transaction.
-- TROCADERO SELLS LONDON COMPLEX BACK TO BURFORD

Leisure group Trocadero has sold its London complex to Burford Holdings less than two years after purchasing it from the same group. Trocadero has warned of difficulties at its Segaworld theme park and delays in opening two attractions at the Trocadero Centre will lead to a first half trading loss. The sale leaves Trocadero with 73m stg in cash to develop its intellectual property rights business.
-- BROWN SETS OUT WIDESCALE OVERHAUL OF CORPORATE TAX

UK chancellor Gordon Brown unveiled his 1997 Budget on Wednesday, which included backdated cuts in corporation tax and the abolition of dividend tax credits paid to pension funds and companies. Corporate taxation rates will be imposed upon dividends paid on shares and held as trading assets, leading to significantly higher taxes for market makers and 'hedge funds'. The corporate tax is part of an anti-tax avoidance package which is hoped to raise 565m stg next year.
-- POLLUTERS COULD BE HIT BY NEW 'GREEN TAXES'

The Treasury is considering proposals to tax North Sea oil producers, mineral extractors and companies which pollute the sea, as Gordon Brown declared the environment was at the core of the government's objectives for the tax system. Brown announced a series of reviews into environmental taxation which could lead to new tax measures in next spring's Budget.
-- TAX BREAKS IN BUDGET TO BENEFIT CINEMA

Sir Sydney Samuelson, the British Film Commissioner, has graciously welcomed a Budget clause which denotes a 100 percent write off of production and acquisition costs for film makers and producers working on pictures with budgets less than 15m stg. Samuelson called the decision a 'wonderful boost' and now expects to see an increase in investment from domestic and foreign film makers. Heritage secretary Chris Smith, 'Wilde' producer Marc Samuelson, and Sir David Puttnam have also shown a positive reaction to the tax break.
-- TWO TRANCHE 'WINDFALL TAX' IS WELCOMED

Details of the much speculated upon windfall tax were released by Gordon Brown in Wednesday's Budget speech. In all, 28 companies will be affected by the levy which will raise about 5.2bn stg, including British Telecom, the British Airports Authority and Railtrack. Water and electricity utilities will pay nearly three-quarters of the bill and have welcomed a decision to split the tax into a two tranche system,
payable on December 1 this year and December 1 1998.
-- SURPRISE ABOLITION OF NORTH SEA LEVY WILL BENEFIT CENTRICA

Centrica, the demerged gas supply and trading arm of British Gas GAS.L, appears set to benefit from the government decision to abolish North Sea gas levies which currently prevent BG from making windfall profits at the low cost site. Centrica expressed disappointment at its inclusion in the windfall tax, but the levy on it should be offset by profits from the field. Chancellor Gordon Brown believes the abolition of the North Sea levies will directly affect consumers as gas bills for 18.5m
customers are expected to be reduced by about two per cent.
-- SCOPE OF 'WELFARE TO WORK' PLAN IS WIDENED

The government's welfare-to-work programme, which will make use of the 5.2bn stg raised from the windfall tax, will be extended to include single parents and those receiving incapacity and disability benefits not in the labour market and those not registered as long-term unemployed. Of the 5.2bn stg, 3.1bn stg will be used in a 'new deal' for the young jobless unemployed for over six months and a further 350m stg for the long-term adult unemployed. About 500m stg will be set aside as
an unallocated reserve.
-- BT PHONE MAY REPLACE SWITCHBOARDS

British Telecom has combined the latest cordless telephone technology with digital cellular service to develop a new mobile telephone service which combines fixed line and mobile operations in one service. The new service, to be called OnePhone, is being developed in conjunction with Sweden's Ericsson and is undergoing tests in selected BT offices, with business service hoped to be introduced in the spring and residential service planned for next year for the phone which
will cost about 200 pounds stg.
-- AT&T TO SEEK ALLIANCES WITH STET, UNISOURCE

AT&T, Stet and the Unisource partnership have unveiled plans for a strategic alliances designed to strengthen European and Latin American operations. The partnership will involve Stet and AT&T working together to offer services to large international customers, then Stet taking a 'significant' stake in AT&T and forming a pan-European joint venture to be organised by AT&T and Unisource. Stet chairman Guido Rossi hopes the deal can be completed before the end of the year.
